summary.headline: JSW Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore, but PAT fell 11% to INR328 crore on forex losses and Fujairah's nil contribution.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore and operating EBITDA rose 11% to INR674 crore in Q2 FY27. Port EBITDA was flat at INR594 crore, with margin compressing to 49.4% from 53.1%, as Fujairah contributed nothing and coal terminals diluted mix. Logistics EBITDA more than tripled to INR81 crore, with the rail rake fleet raised to 78 from 42. PBT fell to INR431 crore from INR463 crore on unrealised forex losses and higher depreciation, and PAT fell to INR328 crore from INR369 crore. Management held the FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore, while revising logistics EBITDA margin guidance up to 28% from 24%.

segments.name: Ports
segments.commentary: Q2 cargo of 29.4 mt vs 28.9 mt (+2% YoY; India +8%). Third-party share 45%; India third-party volumes +13% YoY, total third-party +1% due to nil Fujairah. Port EBITDA margin 49.4% vs 53.1%.

segments.name: Logistics (Navkar and rail)
segments.commentary: Navkar domestic cargo 459,000 MT (+16% YoY); EXIM 88,000 TEUs (+12% YoY). Logistics revenue about INR279 crore, of which Navkar about INR223 crore. Rake fleet 42 to 78 by quarter-end; 110 targeted by March 2027.

segments.name: Fujairah Liquid Terminal (international)
segments.commentary: Nil volume and EBITDA contribution; about INR16 crore EBITDA loss in H1 FY27 from fixed overheads. Eight tanks awaiting commissioning, with operations targeted for early November 2026, but storage demand has weakened.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of about INR2,950-3,000 crore retained: port EBITDA now about INR2,550-2,560 crore (vs INR2,600 crore earlier), logistics slightly above INR400 crore.

Logistics FY27 EBITDA margin guidance raised to 28% from 24%, with the INR400 crore EBITDA target unchanged; logistics revenue guidance cut because rake income is now netted for haulage, which lifts margin.
FY27 capex expected at INR5,000-6,000 crore; overall FY27-FY28 capex guidance of INR16,500 crore unchanged.
H2 FY27 India volume growth expected at 8-10% YoY; Jaigarh and Dharamtar combined about 46 mt for FY27.
Jatadhar port berths and Panamax-level dredging by March 2027, with cargo handling from end-March or April 2027 and Cape-size handling in Q3 FY28.
Port capacity roadmap of 300 mtpa by FY28 and 400 mtpa by FY30 retained.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex about INR8,250 crore to September 2026, including INR1,500 crore in Q2; H1 FY27 capex about INR2,100 crore.
A further INR6,000 crore committed via orders; outstanding capex creditors about INR950 crore; total committed capex about INR14,250 crore.
Rake fleet 78 today; 6 more to be operational in Nov-Dec, 32 more to be delivered in H2, reaching 110 by March 2027. Long-term target about 267-270 rakes (157 container, 110 LSFTO), expected to rise.
Oman and Murbe projects: work expected to start in Q4 FY27. Oman bids due mid-November 2026; Keni awaiting environment clearance, about 3-4 months more.
Slurry pipeline about 88% complete, commissioning by March 2027. Dharamtar mechanisation by Q4 FY27, Jaigarh by Q1 FY28.
Kolkata: 30-year concession signed for 13 mtpa Outer Container Terminal at NSD Dock; interim operations started at the 6.3 mtpa Kolkata container terminal.
demand_pricing: Paradip iron ore volumes fell after a transport moisture limit disrupted exports from August to September; about 8 lakh tonnes stock built up at the terminal by end-September.
Fujairah storage demand has fallen sharply as ships are avoiding the area; management is watching this and sees long-term potential.
Captive steel cargo is sticky; the next group cargo step-up is tied to Dolvi expansion.
Paradip Coal, Ennore Bulk, Tuticorin and Mangalore are driving third-party growth; a 30-day Tuticorin berth shutdown is planned in H2.
Jatadhar: 690 m of berth built, against about 3.5 km of waterfront; EC for 52 mt; management says capacity can reach 100-120 mt with more machinery and a common rail corridor taking about 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Rake business revenue, EBITDA margin and whether revenue scales linearly with rakes?
qa_highlights.answer: Rake EBITDA margin about 90% because only premium and rebate are booked as revenue, with haulage netted off. Overall logistics margin about 28%. Management said LSFTO rake revenue is linear with rake count; container rake revenue depends on volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Fujairah restart timing and volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Eight tanks are under FOIS commissioning, with final permission expected around 29 October and operations targeted for the first week of November. Demand for storage has fallen, so the pace is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the FY27 logistics revenue guidance and the margin guidance changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Haulage is now netted off, so revenue guidance falls while EBITDA is kept. Q1 and Q2 margin was about 30% against a 25% guidance assumption. Margin guidance is revised for FY27 only; the FY28 call will be made with Q3 or Q4 results.

qa_highlights.question: Other income jump and whether it normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: The jump is interest on QIP proceeds of about INR6,400 crore net, held in mutual funds and FDs. It will persist until drawn down for capex.

qa_highlights.question: Fujairah EBITDA history and insurance claim status?
qa_highlights.answer: Fujairah contributed about INR250 crore EBITDA in FY26 and INR134 crore in H1 FY26. Insurance claims are under assessment and await a war declaration; capex to rebuild storage is the priority over loss-of-profit claims.

qa_highlights.question: Jaigarh delays and Jatadhar cargo start timing?
qa_highlights.answer: LPG berth operations to start by March 2027; tankage delayed by a change in planning authority, now resolved, with completion around Q3 FY28. Jatadhar cargo handling from end-March or April 2027, Cape-size in Q3 FY28.

risks_watch: Fujairah: whether the eight tanks start in November 2026 and whether demand returns; insurance claim outcome pending a war declaration.
FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR2,950-3,000 crore needs H2 port EBITDA and rake ramp-up; rake deliveries of 32 in H2 are the key dependency.
Keni port environment clearance is expected in 3-4 months, which may delay that project.
Rising finance costs from ROU/finance-lease rakes and forex losses on rupee depreciation continue to pressure PBT.
Port margin pressure from low-margin coal volumes; Jaigarh volume recovery expected in H2.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the consolidated FY27 EBITDA target and the rake ramp-up, but cautious on Fujairah, which management described as fluid. Evasive on FY28 logistics margins, which were deferred to Q3 or Q4 results.
key_quotes: So from a logistics perspective, we are confident that we should be in a position to achieve slightly above INR400 crores in terms of EBITDA.
Long-term prospects, extremely bullish, but immediate prospects, we have to wait and watch.
So these numbers are fixed on basis of the number of terminals that we start to get in place.
